messages:
maya.reps: Heads-up: Verdant wants to swap out CompetitorX with Redwood. Key asks: drop-in proxy (no client changes), how to map their size_class billing to per-token, strict determinism for a subset of calls (audit/regulatory), SCIM + BYOK, and any response deltas that would break their ranking/scoring. Who can run presales?
diego.se: I'll own the proxy. They use an async webhook flow sometimes (POST -> immediate 202, then webhook callback). We should preserve that contract. Also they rely on a 'size_class' param (S/M/L) that maps to max tokens currently.
annis.eng: Technical risks: tokenizer differences (especially with multibyte emoji and long hyphenated product SKUs) can change token counts and char offsets; sampling defaults differ so determinism req means we should force deterministic sampling (top_k=1 / temperature=0) on those calls. Stop-sequence handling may differ with CompetitorX using literal "\\n--END--" markers.
hannah.solutions: Parity plan: 1) collect 250 representative requests (including async webhook flows and deterministic-only calls), 2) run A/B vs CompetitorX and Redwood (std + quantized), 3) measure: a) major-regression rate on intent/classification, b) token distribution per size_class, c) offset-alignment failures for entity spans, d) webhook latency/ordering.
mark.security: Security checklist: SCIM + SAML, BYOK (AWS/GCP KMS) for keys at rest, optional HSM requirement for audit keys, IP allowlist for webhook endpoints, signed SOC2 addendum, and EU data residency for EU customers. Need their legal/compliance contacts and sample IP ranges.
sec-bot: mark.security uploaded Verdant security questionnaire draft (link: https://security.redwood.example/verdant/494500).
diego.se: Adapter mapping for sync call (CompetitorX -> Redwood):
```
// CompetitorX sync request
POST /v1/generate
{ "prompt": "Extract entities...", "size_class": "M", "stop": "\\n--END--" }

// Redwood translation
POST /v1/completions
{ "model": "redwood-gen-2", "input": "Extract entities...", "max_output_tokens": 120, "stop_sequences": ["\\n--END--"], "sampling": { "temperature": 0 } }
```
Note: map size_class to max_output_tokens via sample mapping; for deterministic flows set sampling.temperature=0 and seed where supported.
maya.reps: They also use a character-offset based span in their scorer (not token-based). How do we reduce offset drift?
annis.eng: We can add an offset-mapping shim that attempts char->token alignment using tokenizer heuristics and fuzzy substring matching. Will catch ~95% of cases but edgecases remain (combining/normalization differences). Recommend adding a lightweight sanity-check step: if mapping confidence low, surface a telemetry flag to their scoring to fallback to fuzzy-match mode. Include test vectors with emojis and accented characters.
hannah.solutions: Billing mapping: collect samples per size_class -> compute avg tokens_per_response and tokens_per_month = avg_tokens * monthly_calls. Example: if size_class M -> avg 140 tokens, monthly 100k calls -> 14M tokens -> multiply by per-token rate. I'll provide a Colab to let their finance tweak per-token rates and monthly volume.
mark.security: For BYOK & HSM: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via dedicated contract (we rotate wrapped keys); Private/Dedicated can use customer KMS or on-prem HSM. Will include cipher-suite and key-lifecycle notes in SA doc.
diego.se: Acceptance criteria proposal: 1) parity suite (250 cases) <= 2.5% major regressions; 2) deterministic endpoints produce identical outputs vs CompetitorX for deterministic subset (modulo whitespace norm) in >=98% of cases; 3) webhook ordering P95 within 350ms of callback for async flows; 4) billing projection within 10% after sampling; 5) security questionnaire signed.
maya.reps: Timeline? Verdant wants an internal customer demo in 11 business days.
hannah.solutions: Proposed schedule: day 0-1: creds + security kickoff; day 2-4: implement proxy (preserve async contract) + smoke tests; day 5-7: run parity & billing sampling; day 8-9: remediate deltas (normalizer + offset shim); day 10-11: prep demo and dry-run.
annis.eng: Engineering caveats: (a) deterministic checks require locking sampling params and seeding — floating point rounding across runtimes can still cause tiny diffs, (b) emoji/multibyte handling is a known source of offset mismatch; include targeted tests, (c) async webhook retries and idempotency: ensure our adapter surfaces idempotency keys to avoid double-scoring.
maya.reps: @mark.security please start the SA doc and get their compliance contact. @diego.se spin the proxy repo and post initial smoke logs here. I'll keep legal on standby for SOC2 addendum.
mark.security: On it. Please DM their compliance & IP ranges.
diego.se: Will open the proxy repo and share link + smoke logs by COB tomorrow.
maya.reps: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the canonical POC channel. :rocket:
